reviews: Share the closed read-only RPC lifecycle; keep client and browser credentials separate; preserve request ownership across cancellation, disconnect and expiry.
Reproduce and tighten hostname boundaries; keep user reports separate from independently evidenced threats; retain exact-host history and existing exceptions.
Verify both transports in all three browsers, unchanged saved configuration and ad blocking, native rule boundaries, final package/server hashes, cleanup and setup documentation.
findings: A new raw URL negative fixture exposed query/fragment characters being admitted into the requested-host regex; authority characters were restricted before final native runs.
The dropped-response test initially treated its intentional ECONNRESET as a test failure; it now waits for close while retaining the assertion that the pending browser read survives.

A CLI process exceeded the test-only three-second startup deadline during concurrent suites. The startup allowance is now ten seconds with explicit spawn-error reporting; HTTP body and browser-read deadlines are unchanged.

One initial Chrome run stopped at manager startup before MCP checks, with no recorded runtime exception. A Firefox stdio attempt timed out in browsingContext.getTree before extension checks. Independent final runs passed; the original startup causes were not established.
Chrome selected the earlier exact pxl rule instead of the overlapping new domain rule. The native assertion now accepts either explicit requested block and separately tests a new WebSocket subdomain.

Firefox testMatchOutcome returned no match for a raw wss URL. The fixture now uses the existing HTTP(S)-handshake representation and records both URLs. All three full suites also exercise a real local WebSocket with the new rule pattern aliased to localhost, including successful control and restore handshakes.

The first real Firefox WebSocket denial passed its block/restore assertions but its intentional connection error reached the unexpected-error check. The fixture now retains that exact local endpoint message as an expected network error, constrained to the owned page context; unrelated errors still fail.
limits: Native test clients exercised real server processes and browser approval. Personal Codex registration and an end-to-end Codex model tool call were not performed.
HTTP is authenticated loopback-only configured bearer access, not OAuth, TLS, a remote service or a defense against software already controlling the same user account.

The new domain entry records the user report and request, without live-site visits or an independent malware reputation claim. It belongs to the ad layer and respects explicit allow/pause preferences.
Offline fixtures verify these source snapshots and do not establish universal live-site protection.
